newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha flat, eyes on LSWR arbitrage to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha flat, eyes on LSWR arbitrage to U.S..

text.p: Naphtha prices barely budged in afternoon Tokyo trade on Tuesday with traders waiting for fresh trading incentives from overseas markets after market holidays in London and New York on Monday, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half August was notionally assessed at $218.50/219.00 per tonne, little changed from late Monday's $218.50/219.50.
Second-half July was quoted even with first-half August.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders' attention centred on potential arbitrage opportunities to the United States.
With price differentials between NYMEX crude futures and Indonesian LSWR cargoes wide enough, June LSWR sales to the U.S. could be imminent, traders said.
The possible arbitrage would boost sentiment in regional fuel oil as the size of one LSWR cargo destined for the U.S. is usually as large as one million barrels, they said.

In middle distillates, one Japanese oil firm said it had bought about 30,000 tonnes of jet A-1 for late June delivery to Chiba, near Tokyo. The firm declined to disclose the exact price, but said the level was a slight discount to the mean of Japanese quotes. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
